tagline: North from Cumberland Gap on Daniel Boone's old trace.
intro: The road starts at Middlesboro, a mile west of Cumberland Gap, in a town platted in 1888 inside a meteorite crater and pitched to English backers as a Magic City of 250,000. From there US 25E runs north through Pineville and Barbourville, and US 25 carries on by London and Mount Vernon to Berea and its crafts, about 94 miles.

Daniel Boone and 35 axmen cut the first trail in March 1775. It was steep, rough and narrow, fit only for walkers and riders, and a wagon road did not open until 1796. Modern highways follow much of the line.

moments.title: Cumberland Gap
moments.text: The V-shaped pass at 1,631 feet that let the settlers through, with Pinnacle Overlook standing 900 feet above it on the north side.

moments.title: Pineville
moments.text: Founded in 1781 as Cumberland Ford, where the Wilderness Road crossed the river, on a strip of land between the Cumberland and Pine Mountain.

moments.title: Renfro Valley
moments.text: John Lair's barn dance opened here in 1939 and gave Hank Williams and Red Foley early stage time. The Sunday Gatherin' has gone out over the radio every week since 1943.

sources.label: FHWA America's Byways, Wilderness Road Heritage Highway
